review_notes: I read the whole file with the simp interface in mind. It declares no @[simp] or @[simps] lemmas. The only attributes are @[fun_prop] on the measurability results, namely measurable_fderiv, measurable_fderiv_apply_const, measurable_deriv, measurable_derivWithin_Ici and measurable_derivWithin_Ioi. Those attributes are not simp rules, and nothing in them points to a loop or a competing rule. The internal definitions A, B and D in both auxiliary namespaces are unfolded explicitly with `simp only [D, ...]` or `simp [B]`, so they do not need simp attributes. The proofs use simp, simp only and convert! followed by simp in routine ways: mem_univ and and_true after convert!, derivWithin_Ioi_eq_Ici, and differentiableWithinAt_Ioi_iff_Ici. I found no sign that these are fragile, that a rewrite points the wrong way, or that a canonical simp lemma is missing. I did not open the Mathlib lemmas those simp calls use, and I could not run Lean, so I cannot say how robust the simp calls are in practice. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
